name: Jerahmeel
overview: Jerahmeel is a male figure mentioned in the book of Jeremiah. He is uniquely identified as the son of King Jehoiakim (also called Eliakim) and is noted for being sent to seize Baruch and the prophet Jeremiah. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jerahmeel means 'G-d [El] will have compassion.' This proper name reflects a meaningful attribute of God, though it was not given directly by God according to the record. The biblical reference for this name is Jeremiah 36:26.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jerahmeel as the son of Eliakim, who is identified as King Jehoiakim. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jerahmeel's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his role as an agent of the king, specifically being sent to seize Baruch and Jeremiah. This action places him within the context of opposition to the prophetic ministry during Jehoiakim's reign. His mention highlights the challenges faced by God's messengers in delivering His word during a turbulent period in Judah's history.
